correctness.rationale: The density and conditional CDF are explicitly differentiated. Admissibility is equivalent to a bounded rank-one product; stochastic increase is decided by the sign of alpha(1-2u)^2-2. The SI correlation envelope strictly increases up to alpha=2. For larger alpha, the derivative of an exact one-variable integral envelope has one and only one zero since Q prime equals s squared times (2s squared minus 1) times exp(-s squared). The limiting and degeneracy cases are stated. Symbolic and numerical checks reproduce the exact expressions and values; uniqueness comes from analysis, not numerical search.

value.rationale: The sharp SI ceiling reveals a rigorous dependence-versus-conditional-monotonicity cost in a copula proposed for achieving higher dependence, and supplies an attained boundary usable when restricting statistical dependence models. The two-branch rank nonidentification is a structural consequence of the continuous shape envelope. Exact optimization alone would be only a small numerical refinement of the old table; necessity of the stochastic-order loss is the substantive mathematical contribution.
